A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure raise the share of lung cancer patients who get curative-intent treatment, and by how much?
Measure: Thoracic surgeon reviews every decision not to operate. A thoracic surgeon from the university hospital sits in the county lung meeting every week and gives a second opinion before a stage I-II patient is refused surgery. Counties without their own thoracic surgeon decide about surgery without one today.
effect_summary_en: An English observational study (Lau et al. 2013) found resection rates of 20.0% in hospitals where surgeons were based versus 11.6% in peripheral hospitals, and the biggest gains where specialist surgeons were added; the abstract does not isolate the effect of a surgeon reviewing every decision not to operate.
supported_en: Lau et al. (J Thorac Oncol 2013) report resection rates of 20.0% in hospitals with a thoracic surgeon on site versus 11.6% in peripheral hospitals in England.
not_supported_en: The pages do not show the 2.4-point gain in curative-intent treatment that comes specifically from a surgeon's second opinion.
in_use_summary_en: The OYS lung cancer care pathway page says the university hospital is responsible for lung cancer multidisciplinary meetings and for surgery and radiotherapy; no page says a thoracic surgeon reviews every no-surgery decision for Lapland patients.
missing_en: No page shows that a thoracic surgeon attends every meeting or gives a second opinion before a stage I-II patient is refused surgery, or that Lapland patients' cases go to the OYS meetings.
summary_en: On its lung cancer care pathway page, OYS (Oulu University Hospital) says it runs the lung cancer multidisciplinary meetings and does all lung cancer surgery. Lapha's (Lapland's) own page says Lapland patients get their radiotherapy at OYS. Neither page says that a thoracic surgeon reviews every decision not to operate. On the effect, an English observational study (Lau et al. 2013) found resection rates of 20.0% in hospitals with surgeons on site versus 11.6% in peripheral hospitals, but it does not measure a surgeon's second opinion on its own.
unanswered_en: I found no page saying whether a thoracic surgeon attends the meetings that discuss Lapland patients, or whether those cases are discussed at OYS or in Rovaniemi.
